summary: Yutaka Yoshida works in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tokyo University of Education, Hitotsubashi University, and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Hitotsubashi University (1983–2018) and Kyoto University (circa 2006–2020).

Yutaka Yuda was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Hajime Nakamura and at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He held academic posts at Kyoritsu University of Pharmacy (1969) and Kanagawa University (1975–2003).

Yutang Lin was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics. He studied at St. John's University, Harvard University, and the University of Leipzig under August Conrady, later holding a post at Peking University circa 1923 to 1926.

Yuto Kawamura is an Indology and linguistics scholar. Kawamura served as a postdoctoral fellow at Kyoto University (2015–2018) and held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 2013–2020) and the University of Oxford (attested 2019).

Yuzo Mizoguchi was a Sinology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Nagoya University under Yoshitaka Iriya, and Kyushu University. He held professorships at Saitama, Hitotsubashi, Tokyo, Daito Bunka, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

Yün-hua Jan was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. A student of Tan Yun-shan, he was a research fellow at Visva-Bharati University in 1953 and later served as a professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).

Yōzō Taniyama is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He held positions at International Buddhist University (circa 2004–2007), St. Thomas University, Japan (circa 2007–2010), Sophia University (circa 2010–2012), and Tohoku University (circa 2012).

Zarawar Khan is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA and PhD at the University of Peshawar. He served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat, attested from 2019 to 2022.
Zawgyi was a linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Rangoon under Pe Maung Tin from circa 1924 to 1929. He later studied at the University of Dublin from circa 1934 to 1936.

Zayn Kassam is a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at McGill University. Kassam held appointments at Pomona College beginning in 1995, the Institute of Ismaili Studies (fellow in 1998; director in 2023), and the Pacific Basin Institute.

Zeff Bjerken is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez, Jr., among other teachers. He held an attested post at the College of Charleston in 2001.

Zellig Harris was a linguist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1928 to 1934. He subsequently taught at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1934 to 1979 and held a post at Columbia University.

Zeng Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. Yang was a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under Jinhua Chen.
Zenjo Inoue was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji from circa 1934 to 1937.
Zenkei Shibayama was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held academic posts at Hanazono University from circa 1946 to 1968 and at Otani University from circa 1948 to 1951.
Zenno Ikuno is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. at the University of Tokyo and held a post at Asia University, attested in 1982.

Zenno Ishigami was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He held posts at Taisho University (1963–2000), Jodo Shu Research Institute (circa 2002–2006), Shukutoku Junior College (2002–2014), Shukutoku University (2014), and Dongguk University.

Zennosuke Tsuji was a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar. After studying at the University of Tokyo (circa 1896–1899), he held posts there (circa 1911–1938), at the University of the Sacred Heart (circa 1948–1954), and at Rissho University (circa 1949–1955).

Zenryu Tsukamoto was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Bukkyo, Shukyo, and Kyoto universities under multiple mentors, later serving Kyoto University (1949–1974), the Kyoto National Museum (1961–1972), and Kacho Junior College (1973).

Zesho Machida was a Buddhist studies scholar. He held an attested post at Minobusan Okunoin Shishinkaku in 1990 and served as professor emeritus at Minobusan University, attested between 1996 and 2001.
